title: Hyrule Warriors: Age of Calamity
description: Hyrule Warriors: Age of Calamity revisits the world and characters of Breath of the Wild through the large-scale musou action formula. Players take command of Link, Zelda, the Champions, and other fighters across cinematic battlefields packed with enemies, captains, bosses, and mission objectives. The game also received an Expansion Pass that adds new characters, stages, and challenges.

nintendoNotes: Nintendo sells both the base game and a separate Expansion Pass. This extraction maps the user's Special and Deluxe pricing tiers to Expansion Pass-aware variants.

gameplayPillars.title: Large-scale battlefield action
gameplayPillars.description: Fight through waves of enemies while capturing keeps, defeating bosses, and protecting allied positions.

gameplayPillars.title: Breath of the Wild cast and setting
gameplayPillars.description: The game draws heavily from the characters, aesthetics, and regions of Breath of the Wild.

gameplayPillars.title: Distinct hero movesets
gameplayPillars.description: Each playable character has unique attacks, special mechanics, and combo styles that keep battles varied.

gameplayPillars.title: Story-driven campaign
gameplayPillars.description: Unlike some musou titles that rely mostly on loose scenarios, Age of Calamity presents a cinematic story campaign with frequent cutscenes.

gameplayPillars.title: Expansion Pass content
gameplayPillars.description: Post-launch content adds more weapons, characters, and challenges for players who want a broader package.

worldSummary: Age of Calamity reframes Zelda lore through wide battlefields, hero swapping, hordes of enemies, and a campaign that tries to connect directly to Breath of the Wild's world and themes.

storyChapters.title: Hyrule prepares for war
storyChapters.body: The kingdom mobilizes as Calamity Ganon's threat grows, gathering heroes and warriors from across Hyrule.

storyChapters.title: Recruit the Champions and allies
storyChapters.body: Link and Zelda join forces with the Champions and other important characters to resist the coming calamity.

storyChapters.title: Fight across major regions
storyChapters.body: Campaign stages send the player across familiar areas with objectives, bosses, and large enemy forces.

storyChapters.title: Unlock stronger tools and movesets
storyChapters.body: Progression rewards weapon upgrades, side missions, and additional playable characters.

storyChapters.title: Reach the climax of the conflict
storyChapters.body: The later chapters push toward a large-scale showdown tied to the fate of Hyrule.

features: Breath of the Wild-themed musou action
Strong roster variety and flashy combat
Expansion Pass support for premium variants
Good option for players who enjoy battlefield-heavy action

faq.q: Does Age of Calamity have DLC?
faq.a: Yes. Nintendo released an Expansion Pass that adds new content, which is why this extraction includes Special and Deluxe variant tiers.
Yes. It supports local cooperative play for up to two players on a single system.

faq.q: Is this an open-world Zelda game?
faq.a: No. It is a mission-based musou action game, not a free-roaming open-world structure like Breath of the Wild.

faq.q: Can I enjoy it without playing Breath of the Wild?
faq.a: Yes, but familiarity with the Breath of the Wild cast and setting will make many story moments more meaningful.

faq.q: Why are the online account tiers more expensive?
faq.a: That follows the store's pricing structure, while the gameplay content remains tied to the base game and its optional Expansion Pass.

verdictPros: Fun musou combat with a strong Zelda theme
Good roster variety and flashy special attacks
Local co-op is a welcome feature
Expansion Pass adds value to premium tiers
Cinematic story framing appeals to BOTW fans
verdictCons: Performance can dip during very busy battles
Mission structure is less free than mainline Zelda games
Musou combat is not for everyone
Some story expectations depend on player familiarity with BOTW
Grinding side content may feel repetitive for completionists
